summary: Round r1 (restricted network; data hosts blocked). The agent's single WebSearch located primary procedure documents for IMF and World Bank crisis instruments: the 2025 IMF factsheets on the RFI and RCF, the RFI factsheet page, the IDA Immediate Response Mechanism page, the World Bank guidance note on Contingent Emergency Response Components, the note on Operation of the Crisis Response Window, and IEG's CRW lessons synthesis. Together with register/upstream leads (IMF Nepal ECF extension and 2026 Article IV, IDA terms and products 2026, WB CPF, ADB CPS, CDP crisis assessment, NDRRMA, PDNA precedents, MoFA consular releases, AMIS/DCR) and leads marked 'URL from general knowledge - unverified' (CCRT, RSF, PRGT eligibility, Cat DDO, WB crisis toolkit, ADB APDRF and emergency policy, CERF, FTS, ReliefWeb, INSARAG), 43 leads are recorded. Q1 (documented procedures governing crisis financing and coordination) is set up as 17 procedure maps, each with trigger/eligibility, steps to verify, decision body, documents, terms, time-to-disbursement and Nepal applicability, all pending. A hypothetical sequencing design links the maps to scenarios S01, S04, S05 and S10 for 27E. No numbers recorded; search-snippet figures were deliberately not used. Nothing here represents any government or institution's decisions.

findings.claim: Method: procedure maps are built from the institution's own procedure documents; the step outlines in r1 are retrieval checklists from lead titles and general knowledge and are not evidence.
Method: rules on concurrent use (e.g. IMF emergency facility alongside an ECF arrangement) are taken from the latest official policy text and dated; factsheet summaries are cross-checks.

Crisis-coordination simulations are hypothetical sequencing exercises; they do not predict or represent decisions of the Government of Nepal, the IMF, the World Bank, ADB, the UN or any other government.

data_gaps: Retrieved RFI/RCF factsheets and the underlying IMF policy papers on emergency financing and concurrent use with PRGT arrangements (current vintage).
Current IDA-cycle CRW operating rules (the located operation note's cycle must be confirmed) and Crisis Preparedness and Response Toolkit documents.
List of Nepal World Bank operations with CERCs and their operations manuals; IRM readiness documents; any Cat DDO.
ADB APDRF and Disaster and Emergency Assistance Policy texts (general-knowledge URLs) and Nepal precedent use.
Nepal DRRM Act 2074 official text and National Disaster Response Framework (no document-level lead).
SAARC currency swap framework press releases/agreement and any NRB swap agreement (landing pages only).
Nepal's IMF emergency financing history (country page lending table) and documented disbursement timelines for past crises.

assumptions.text: Procedure maps use the latest official policy text; factsheets are cross-checks, and vintages are recorded because rules change across IDA cycles and IMF reviews.
IMF access limits are recorded as percent of quota (unit 'percent'); SDR amounts are not recorded until a unit code exists.
World Bank periods are recorded on the Bank's fiscal year (July-June), IMF on calendar dates, and Nepal records on Nepal FY; no conversion without a documented method.

challenges.text: Add an SDR money unit code (e.g. SDR_current_mn) to src/economic_model/units.py and catalog ids for IEG, UN OCHA/CERF, INSARAG and ADB APDRF; 27D cannot record IMF access in SDR otherwise.

programme_register should record whether the ECF extension approved in 2026 changes rules for concurrent emergency financing (RCF alongside ECF) and whether Nepal has CERC-bearing operations; PM-02, PM-03 and PM-07 depend on it.
PRGT eligibility and IDA terms may shift with the LDC graduation timeline; please record the dates on which Nepal's category under each institution would be reviewed, if documented.
PM-14 needs the DRRM Act 2074 official text and the National Disaster Response Framework; if 13A/13C hold these, please add document-level leads.

uncertainty: High: procedure documents were located but not retrieved, so rules, limits and timelines are unverified; facility rules change frequently (temporary access increases, IDA cycle changes), so a retrieved document may already be superseded. Nepal's eligibility for several instruments depends on pending upstream items (PRGT eligibility, IDA terms, CERC-bearing operations). Many ADB/UN leads are general-knowledge URLs that may not resolve.

procedure_maps.question: Q1 What documented procedures govern crisis financing and coordination?
procedure_maps.method: For each mechanism: retrieve the governing procedure document (factsheet, policy paper, operational guidance, legal text) and the latest vintage; extract trigger/eligibility, steps, decision body, documents, terms, and any documented timelines; then record Nepal's applicability from Nepal-specific records (IMF country page and staff reports, WB CPF/project documents, ADB CPS, NDRRMA/Law Commission texts). Procedure vintage is recorded because facility rules change across IDA cycles and IMF reviews. Where two documents disagree (e.g. factsheet vs policy paper), both are kept and the later official policy text is flagged for 00B.

coordination_simulation.design: Hypothetical crisis-coordination simulations (tabletop logic, not forecasts) will sequence the procedure maps under scenarios S01, S04, S05 and S10: which instruments are eligible given documented trigger conditions, the order of requests, documents each requires, and the documented time-to-disbursement ranges once retrieved. No probabilities are assigned; no government's choices or intentions are asserted.

scenario_sequences.scenario: S01 Middle East conflict (energy, migrant employment, remittances)

coordination_simulation.outputs_to_27E: eligibility matrix (instrument x scenario), sequencing constraints (e.g. rules on concurrent IMF facilities), documentary prerequisites that must exist before a crisis (CERC manuals, IRM readiness, Cat DDO), and data gaps.
coordination_simulation.hypothetical_label: All arrangements discussed are hypothetical research constructs; this work does not state or represent the actual position or private intentions of any government.
